review_notes: Applying the principal-question hierarchy, Table 2 all observations is retained as the principal regression for the substantive question of whether annual cash effective tax rates predict long-run cash effective tax rates. The paper explicitly describes this predictive assessment as one of its core objectives; the CASH ETR measures are deterministic ratios and require no fitted construction regression.

The Table 2 rows conditional on CASH ETR1 ranges are follow-up partitions. Table 3 changes the dependent variable to next-year CASH ETR1 and examines annual-rate persistence; it is a complementary analysis, not the principal long-run prediction regression. The group-specific Table 3 rows are also not included.
The source does not identify the underlying estimator, and the Table 2 note does not detail the random-draw procedure or selected fiscal year for CASH ETR1 observations; these remain unresolved.
descriptive_reason: Table 1 Panel C, Table 4, and Table 6 report CASH ETR10 and CASH ETR1 data-value summaries. Table 1 samples are broader than the selected random-observation regression; Table 4 industry rows and Table 6 tax-group rows retain their source sample descriptions. Table 6 difference columns are tests rather than variable descriptives and are excluded.
results_review_notes: Selected regression values are from the Table 2 all-observations column. Table 2 condition-specific rows and Table 3 persistence regressions are excluded.

Relevant data-value summaries retained across the paper are Table 1 Panel C distributions, Table 4 industry means, and Table 6 tax-group means. The regression adjustment statistic is not a model variable or data descriptive.

Original Table 4 and Table 6 pages were viewed in a post-prior source follow-up; their retained counts and means are checked against the current PDF crops. Table 5 individual-firm listings and Table 6 difference tests are not variable-descriptive summary rows for this selected model.
